problem: Prior embodied-navigation agents (HAMT, DUET, AZHP, etc.) are task-specific. Each is trained on one dataset with its own design, so it transfers poorly to out-of-domain VLN datasets and cannot handle new tasks such as QA or summarization. Earlier multi-task VLN work (MT-RCM) covered only a few navigation datasets and did not use LLM knowledge.
motivation: Many embodied-navigation datasets are small; CVDN, for example, has only 4.7k training instances. Pretrained LLMs have strong text understanding and have already been adapted to images, video, 3D and manipulation, but not to sequential navigation decisions. If every embodied task can be cast as text generation, one LLM-based model can pool data from all tasks and inherit the LLM's language understanding.
key_idea: Cast every embodied task (VLN, object localization, trajectory summarization, 3D-QA, EQA) as conditional generation with a fine-tuned LLM (Vicuna-7B), using a unified 'schema-based instruction' prompt made of Task / Observation / History / Output-Hint segments that interleave text with ID-tagged visual tokens. Actions are generated as viewpoint or object IDs, and answers as text.
insight:
The pretrained LLM is the main source of gains. With multi-task training, random LLM initialisation versus pretrained Vicuna gives:
- CVDN GP 3.64 vs 5.91
- R2R SPL 40 vs 58
- ScanQA EM 12.4 vs 23.3
(Table 5 rows 2 vs 3). Multi-task data pooling improves every task compared with single-task training: SOON SPL 21.37→28.09, REVERIE SPL 24.10→36.63, CVDN GP 5.54→5.91 (rows 1 vs 3). The gains are largest on datasets with long, complex instructions (CVDN averages 81.6 words). The model still lags DUET/AZHP on REVERIE, whose instructions are short and simple. Pretraining on the large R2R/REVERIE augmented data, which helps prior VLN transformers, gives only small gains here and actually hurts REVERIE (SR 44.56→42.15). The authors conclude that data quality matters more than quantity for an LLM agent. Removing the task and output-hint schema elements drops the summed val-unseen score from 140.45 to 107.49 (Table 6), so explicit task and output schemas are what let one model separate tasks.
method: Scene encoder: a frozen EVA-CLIP-02-Large ViT (428M) takes the [CLS] feature of each of 36 panoramic views. A trainable 2-layer transformer encoder (hidden size 1024) performs multi-view fusion, with angle and GPS information added, producing scene tokens s_i.

Schema-based instruction: the LLM input is assembled from four schemas:
- Task: instruction, dialog, question or summarization query.
- Observation: [Emb(1), s_1, …, Emb(n), s_n] over candidate viewpoints, objects or scene images.
- History: [Emb(1), h_1, …, Emb(t), h_t], the representations of previously selected viewpoints; t = 15/15/30/20 for R2R/REVERIE/CVDN/SOON.
- Output Hint: a text hint describing the expected output.

Generative action prediction: Vicuna-7B-v0 generates the ID of the next viewpoint (candidate 0 = stop), the ID of the target object (option 0 = not exist), or free-form text for answers and summaries. All tasks are trained with a single cross-entropy objective.

Multi-task data: VLN on CVDN, SOON, R2R and REVERIE; object localization from REVERIE/SOON annotations, using ViT-B16 object features from Chen et al.; trajectory summarization built by reversing instruction–trajectory pairs; 3D-QA from ScanQA plus sub-instruction QA built from fine-grained R2R; LLaVA-23k image instruction data. EQA is held out.

Two-stage training: (1) 10k-step teacher-forcing pretraining on all datasets plus R2R (1070k) and REVERIE (20k) augmented data; (2) 5k-step multi-task fine-tuning alternating teacher and student forcing. Batch 64, Adam, lr 3e-5, about 80 h on 8 A100s. The ViT is frozen; the fusion module and LLM are fine-tuned.

Inference: greedy decoding, except sampling at temperature 0.01 on SOON and REVERIE to encourage exploration. EQA is solved zero-shot by chaining the VLN schema (navigate) and the 3D-QA schema (answer).

setting.backbone: Vicuna-7B-v0 (fine-tuned) + frozen EVA-CLIP-02-Large ViT + trainable 2-layer multi-view fusion transformer
setting.training_data: CVDN (4.7k), SOON (27.8k), R2R (14k), REVERIE (10.5k), ScanQA (25.6k), LLaVA-23k, plus R2R augmented data (1070k) and REVERIE augmented data (20k) from HAMT (pretraining stage only). Derived tasks: trajectory summarization from R2R/SOON/REVERIE; object grounding from REVERIE/SOON; QA from fine-grained R2R sub-instructions.
setting.observation: Panoramic RGB (36 views per viewpoint) with view angle / GPS info, plus history of selected-viewpoint features. Candidate-object ViT-B16 features for object localization. Multi-view images of ScanNet scenes for ScanQA.
setting.action_space: Discrete nav-graph viewpoints: generates the candidate direction ID, with 0 = stop. Object ID for localization; free text for QA and summarization.
setting.simulator: Matterport3D simulator (discrete nav graph); ScanNet scenes for ScanQA; MP3D-EQA episodes for zero-shot EQA
setting.privileged: Standard discrete nav-graph candidate viewpoints; dataset-provided candidate object boxes for REVERIE/SOON object grounding. No pre-exploration.

results:
A single NaviLLM model sets the state of the art on:
- CVDN test: GP 7.90 vs 6.13 for VLN-PETL, about 29% relative.
- SOON test: SPL 26.26 vs 25.80 for Meta-Explore.
- ScanQA test w/ objects: EM 26.3 vs 23.5 for ScanQA and 19.1 for 3D-LLM (BLIP2-flant5).
It is comparable on R2R test (SR 68 / SPL 60 vs DUET 69/59 and AZHP 71/60) but trails DUET and AZHP on REVERIE test (SPL 32.33 vs 36.06 / 35.85). In held-out zero-shot transfer it beats the best dataset-specific DUET model on each dataset:
- CVDN: GP 4.46 vs 3.38.
- SOON: SPL 14.29 vs 6.06.
- REVERIE: SR 28.10 vs 24.91.
On MP3D-EQA it reaches 47.78 SR / 35.60 SPL / 44.5 ACC zero-shot.
limitations: Only works on the discrete Matterport3D nav graph (candidate-viewpoint selection); there is no continuous control, VLN-CE evaluation or real robot.

It underperforms specialist models (DUET, AZHP) on REVERIE's short, simple instructions. Object features are not fused with image features, and pretraining on large augmented data brings little or negative gain.
The EQA evaluation uses a manually filtered val subset (849 entries). The 7B LLM makes training (about 80 h on 8 A100s) and per-step inference costly.
